summary: Commercial and civil space operations marked key milestones as Rocket Lab completed its 99th mission by launching a Japanese Earth-observing satellite, while NASA’s ground-based CHAPEA crew completed its simulated long-duration Mars mission. In military defense, the U.S. Space Force is weighing a proposed proliferated cislunar satellite constellation to expand tracking capabilities as service leaders actively appeal for broader commercial industry integration. Commercial momentum continued as Northwood Space secured $375 million in Series C funding at a $2 billion valuation, Stellar Alpina unveiled its new Monarch Orbiter and Morpho Lunar Lander designs, and Hydrosat introduced a high-resolution thermal imaging capability. In scientific research, findings from the James Webb Space Telescope indicate the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS originated in a frigid birthplace, NASA's Hubble Space Telescope identified a shortage of oxygen in nearby dwarf galaxies, and student researchers at Queen's University Belfast discovered elusive Trojan asteroids orbiting near Neptune. Meanwhile, preliminary testing on spacesuit materials suggests Martian dust may prove less abrasive than lunar dust, and satellite operators demonstrated a challenging CubeSat-to-ground laser communications link. Looking ahead, space watchers should keep an eye on preparations for NASA’s upcoming Northrop Grumman CRS-25 commercial resupply mission to the International Space Station.
